Counter-evidence recorded rather than hidden, per this order's explicit instruction: from my own recollection and NOT independently live-verified this session (QC must locate and quote the actual sentences rather than rely on this paraphrase), the same secondary-source family that reports the ruling's derivation finding commonly also records that the Atanasoff-Berry Computer was a fixed-purpose linear-equation solver rather than a general-purpose, programmable machine like ENIAC, that it was never completed to full working spec as originally designed, and that many computer historians dispute how much of ENIAC's actual design the ruling's 'derived' language should be read to cover versus how much was independently developed -- i.e. the derivation finding and a qualification of it appear together in the same source family, which is the specific pattern this order asked not to be hidden.
